_readme: An append-only correction. Applying it records rows in the
event_corrections ledger; it never edits or deletes an observation.
The affected ids are written out literally and not recomputed from a
rule: a correction that can match new events on its own is not a
correction, it is a filter, and it would keep excluding things forever.
Applying this file twice is a no-op -- correction ids are content-
addressed, so the second run writes nothing.
source_bug: rules-v1 types a document by the first rule, in a fixed order, any of whose terms occurs as a raw substring of its casefolded title. 'interest rate' in 'CFTC Issues Final Rule to Modify Clearing Requirement for Canadian Dollar- and Mexican Peso-Denominated Interest Rate Swaps' made a derivatives-clearing rulemaking MONETARY_POLICY. rules-v2, added in be5886b, matches whole words and phrases, weighs every rule and consults the entity's declared event types -- the CFTC declares REGULATION -- and types the same document REGULATION.
notes: This invalidates the original extraction only. The rules-v1 event stays in the store exactly as written, and research stops counting it. The corrected classification is a different event, not a field of this correction: rules-v2's REGULATION event for the same document, 2262b65a8dc36182c9127d2a470b4642bf71d89508e73be553727a0dc4191917, which exists only where an operator re-extracts under rules-v2 and is never pooled with rules-v1. The set is closed: at 2026-09-11 the collected store holds seven rules-v1 events, and this is the only one typed MONETARY_POLICY and the only one whose type came from 'interest rate'. The other six are SEC REGULATION events; the CFTC no-action letter and the BLS release produced no rules-v1 event. Decided from the document's title and the two extractors' rules alone, never from any market outcome.
